To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) STI571 induces Chk2 activation, Cdc2SA degradation, and persistent Cdk-2 inhibitory phosphorylations, leading to growth arrest; 2) STI571-mediated cell growth arrest is independent of p53; 3) STI571-induced cell growth arrest is mediated through a p53-independent Chk2-Cdk2 pathway.
Chk2 is activated by STI571 in myeloid progenitores expressing the bcr-abl kinase, and that Chk2 activation is required for the G1 arrest induced by STI571.
Chk2 is a novel target of STI571 in CML and that the STI571-mediated Chk2 activation is responsible for the G1/earlyS cell cycle arrest of clonal CML myeloid progeni tors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel molecular mechanism of action of STI571 and its potential clinical relevance in the context of the disease.
a molecular pathway that might contribute to the understanding of CML pathogenesis and to the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
a new mechanism of action of STI571 and suggests that the Chk2/Cdc25A/Cdk2 axis is a novel target to overcome STI571 resistance in CML and possibly in other cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Chk2-CDC25A-Cdk pathway is an important player in the response of CML progenitors to STI571 and that its activation is an important component of STI571-induced cell cycle arrest.
the Chk2/Cdc25A pathway is activated by STI571 in CML progenitors to drive cell cycle arrest, a mechanism that may contribute to the clinical efficacy of STI571.
STI571, besides inducing apoptotic death, also induces growth arrest, and that both effects are mediated by the Chk2 pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

STI571 induces cell cycle arrest in CML clonal myelopoietic progenitors through the activation of the Chk2-dependent G(1)/G(0) checkpoint, a pathway complementary with p53 in the regulation of the growth arrest of these cells.
STI571, in addition to induce cell cycle arrest, also induces apoptosis in myeloid cells, and that these two processes are independent of p53.

STI571, by activating the ChK2-CDC25A-Cdk axis, drives late G1 arrest of clonal CML progenitors, thus contributing to the drug antileukaemic efficacy and to the prevention of the emergence of drug-resistant clones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STI571, in addition to its apoptotic effects, also inhibits the growth of clonal myleoid progenitors by activating a cell cycle checkpoint that is complementary to the p53 pathway.
Chk2-Cdk2 axis might represent a novel target for the development of novel therapeutic agents in CML.
